utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Today we continue hearing evidence by video-conference link. Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, good morning to you, and good morning to Your Honours. Before we start the next witness, might I make a clarification for the record from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yesterday, His Honour Judge Harhoff asked me a request with respect to the direction of fire from the residence of the last witness yesterday, Ms. Gotovac, and I had informed the Trial Chamber that it was from her residence south-west and that the origin of fire was Lukavica. In fact, it is south-east from her residence to Lukavica. And the witness that we will be calling, (redacted), will hopefully demonstrate that that is the direction of fire from her residence, as he was involved in the investigation of that incident. So just to make that clarification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, immediately before that is done, just so that everybody in the room is aware, the second witness who is going to appear this morning will not be available before noon I have been told. The Victims and Witness Unit won't be picking her up until that time, and that's because she has a work commitment that she wasn't able to change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may proceed, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Holjan. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That's good. I'd like to ask you some questions then about the statements that you have given as to what happened on the day you were shot and then some extra details about that day. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, first, Mr. Holjan, have you had a chance to read the three statements that you have given about the day you were shot; one to the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1995, one to the Tribunal in 1996, and then the last one to the Tribunal in 2006?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, if I could just ask you a question about those three statements, I see in the first and the second statement, the ones from 1995 and 1996, you said you were sitting on the right-hand side of the tram when you were shot. But in the last statement, from 2006, you were sitting -- you said you were sitting on the left-hand side of the tram when you were shot.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Well, I made a small mistake there. I switched the two sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So could you please clarify for us today exactly what side of the tram you were at when you were shot, the right or the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: We were on the right-hand side of the tram near the door, near the exit door of the tram.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And was he sitting or standing?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Were you sitting or standing, Mr. Holjan; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: We were sitting, sitting on the right-hand side next to the exit door, and that's where we were hit by the armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, apart from what we've just talked about, do you have any other changes you want to make to your statement?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: No. I have nothing to add or change.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Then, Your Honours, if I could, I'd like to tender the Bosnian language statement of Mr. Holjan with 65 ter number 03074, the 1996 statement with ter number 03073, and the 2006 statement with ter number 03072, each as exhibits, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit them.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 03074 becomes P524; 65 ter number 03073 becomes P525; and 65 ter number 03072 becomes P526.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Holjan, because all the previous statements that you have given, with the clarification that you have made, have been admitted as exhibits for the Trial Chamber to study. I only have one more question for you about what happened on the day you were shot. Do you remember whether you heard or you saw any kind of military activity, no matter what, going on around the time and place you were shot?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: There were no military activities going on there. They were holding those cross roads. It was all civilians. There were no military persons there, only civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, thank you very much, Mr. Holjan. Those are all the questions I'm going to ask you, and now the counsel for General Milosevic has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. My name is Branislava Isailovic. I work for the Paris Bar Association, and I am defending the accused, General Dragomir Milosevic. As the Prosecutor has just told you, I'm going to ask you a few questions regarding the statements you gave to the Bosnian police and to the Prosecutor. To begin with, Witness, you have just corrected a detail contained in your statement dated the 25th of April, 2006. You remember this, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, why, on the 25th of April, 2006, you mentioned the left-hand side of the tramway? You said that this was the side of the tram where you were sitting at the time of the incident.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: I corrected it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Witness, what counsel is asking you is to explain why, in the first instance, you said you were sitting on the left-hand side of the tram?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I made a mistake. I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you tell me when did you first realise that you had made a mistake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember the day when I made this mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you were questioned twice. Once on the 14th of April, 1995, you indicated that you were on the right-hand side, as you did today; and on the 22nd of February, 1996, you also indicated that you were on the right-hand side like today. And it was only in 2006, in light of this trial, that you indicated that you were on the left-hand side. So this is my question: Did someone from the Office of the Prosecutor who conducted the interview with you suggest to you that it might have been on this side? Yes or no. I mean the left-hand side of the tram.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you tell us, please, in which direction was the tram heading when you said that the fires were shot from Grbavica? So which -- in which direction was the tram heading?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: The tram was moving from Marindvor in the direction of Novo Sarajevo, New Sarajevo, where my company is located.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And which side of the tram was facing Grbavica, as you said that the shot came from there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: The left side.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you also mention in your statement dated 25th of April, 2006 things which you did not mention in your 1996 statement; namely, in paragraph 12, and this is document P526, the witness's statement dated 26th of April, 2006 -- 25th of April. In paragraph 12, this is on page 3 of the English text and on page 3 of the B/C/S version. Witness, have you read this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: I don't know where exactly the conflict line is in relation to the side from which the shot came. It might have been a thousand metres away up on the hills.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you know at the time of this incident where the confrontation lines were exactly?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: I didn't say where the confrontation line was at the time when what happened happened to us down there in the tram.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: From what I understood, Witness, you had to move around the town quite a bit. This was part of your job, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Well, that's what my job was like. I had to be in town all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember that at the time there was a border which shouldn't be crossed at the time?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: At that time, there were no borders one couldn't cross, because we had to go from the Bascarsija to Cengic Vila all the time, and we had do our work and do our jobs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And when you talk about the neighbourhood of Grbavica, did you quite often to Grbavica during the war?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: I didn't go to Grbavica at all throughout the war, over the Miljacka. We only went on this side to Cengic Vila or Novo Sarajevo, or New Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And what was Miljacka river at the time; in other words, as regards the position of both armies?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: I don't know what the Miljacka represented. The two armies had their own border, but we who were down there didn't know anything about those.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in paragraph 13 of your statement, which we have currently before us, the one dated 25th of April, 2006, you mention the military facilities, or rather, lack of military facilities in that area where the tram was hit. Do you see this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: In the vicinity of the scene where we were attacked by sniper fire, there were absolutely no military facilities or establishments.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, as far as you are concerned, what are military facilities? What does that bring to mind, as far as you're concerned?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: We think there were no soldiers there. Had there been any military establishments, we thought it would have happened because of that army, but that was not so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: When you say -- or when you talk about a military purpose, what you have in mind are soldiers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And you are telling us now that when you had to move around in the town in that area, you saw soldiers of the ABiH army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: We had to -- no. None of us understood anything about those soldiers. We had a lot of work to do. We had to take care of ourselves, our employees, our work, our business, the jobs we had to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm not raising any objection but I'm wondering with respect to the question that my friend asked at page 8 and line 8, "When you had to move around in that area you saw soldiers of the ABiH army." I'm wondering if she can be a little bit more precise because it seems to me that the line of questioning has moved far away from the location at which the attack happened, and it may assist everyone in terms of understanding and clarity if she could be more precise as to what location she is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the area to which you are referring, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, Your Honour, it's becoming an extremely difficult task. You didn't see, you didn't see soldiers, did you? I have to keep an eye on the screen all the time on the transcript. My question was and I can repeat it. And the witness said that he didn't see, and therefore I asked him, "When you moved around you didn't see soldiers of the ABiH army, did you?" That was the question I put in French, and maybe this was translated into B/C/S, "as you saw, didn't you," because in the statement he said that he didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps the witness could answer this question, please, so maybe I could repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You say in your statement that you never saw in this neighbourhood of Marindvor, you never say any ABiH soldiers, did you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you are saying that you didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, in his statement, paragraph 13, he says, "There were absolutely no military establishments in the vicinity of the scene where we were attacked." He doesn't say specifically soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before the question what did he understand by the term "military facilities," he answered by using the word "soldiers," so I hope this is recorded properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you indicate what the position of the tramway was at the time of the impact if I show you a photograph. I have prepared a photograph, but I would, first and foremost, like to ask you this question. Do you remember this well enough? If we are to show you a photograph, would you be able to tell us?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: The tram was near the technical school when this incident happened at Marindvor.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In that case, I think we could show you this photograph, as you will see.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 2914 on the 65 ter list, on the Defence exhibit list, Exhibit 1D, and we shall bring it up on the screen. And I would like the registrar in Sarajevo to show this to you, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see anything here, nothing. I see nothing here. How could I see the tram here? What is this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the photograph also?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's coming. It's coming. I just heard that the witness doesn't see anything, and I wanted to ask him questions using the photographs with the buildings and the tower and so on, but obviously we can't do anything with a picture [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, is this the area -- Witness, please, can you try and find your way in this picture?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Find what?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, find the tracks, in the first place, and the area where the incident occurred. And maybe with the camera in Sarajevo we could see this. The witness could point on the photograph in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really cannot find my way here at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. He can't help you by way of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in your statement, which is now P525, your statement of February 22nd, 1996, on page 2, in the third paragraph, there is a sentence in the middle of this paragraph. You talk of a woman who was seriously wounded, and you heard that she died in hospital. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes. I'm reading it now. What was this? While we were in the street, I saw a wounded woman. This wounded woman was transferred by car to a hospital. She was seriously wounded. And people tried to -- well, I heard she died in hospital. I think five people were wounded. Before we got out of the tram, I did not see anything. There was commotion on the tram; there was panic. I was afraid that none of us would survive.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, who told you that this woman died at hospital?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Well, the passengers who were there with us, who were taken up to the emergency ward.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But you didn't get any confirmation later that this woman had actually died. These were just rumours.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: One last thing. It's the first statement you made right after the fact, April 14, 1995, a month and so after the incident. This is the document which was given the number P524 and the 3074 on the 65 ter list. You don't have to read out loud the entire statement. I'm just asking -- I'll just ask you a question, and if you don't remember you can look at the document. In this document, you say that you were sitting on the right side of the tram, that it was very crowded, and you're talking about bursts of fire that you heard. Could you please tell us more about this, these bursts of fire that you heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, did you hear the question? Can you tell us anything more about the bursts of fire that you heard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what else I'm supposed to say. There were bursts of gun-fire. There were woundings, then people who were wounded were saved, and then they were discharged and they were allowed to go home. That is the only thing I can say to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: When reading this statement, maybe that's the way it is. But I want to ask you a question, because you say that you heard bursts of fire on the left side of the tram. That's what you say, and then --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: -- after that, you say the bullets started to hit the tram. So here is my question. It's a very specific question: Before hearing the bullets hitting the tram, did you hear the bursts of fire first?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: We didn't hear it before that, before the bullets started hitting the tram, and then we fell on to the floor of the tram in order to save ourselves from being hit, and not all of us could save ourselves. Somebody had to get hit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You're absolutely sure of the direction. The bullets were only coming from the left-hand side of the tram. You're sure of that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just a couple of brief questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Holjan, can I ask you some questions based on the answers that you gave to General Milosevic's counsel now.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Holjan, just before your tram was shot, do you remember whether you saw any tanks in the neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA HOLJAN
utterances.text: The tank was up at the crossroads, near the hygiene institute. It was the white UN tank that protected passers-by when they tried to cross from one side of the street to the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Edgerton. Witness, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for giving it and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We now have an enforced break. I should say that even though I understand the difficulties in having witnesses present, every effort should be made to ensure that we make the best and most efficient use of the Chamber's time.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do have one small matter that I can raise since we have a few minutes. I do want to inform the Trial Chamber that we have not forgotten about our -- the request to try to track down Captain Idriz in Kenya. We're continuing to do that. I have been speaking almost on a daily basis with the embassy here, and I -- I was hoping to receive some information yesterday. I didn't. I'm hoping today but certainly by the end of the week I will submit a complete report about all our efforts and the results up to that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are adjourned. Let me clarify then. We are in the hand of the Prosecution apparently, and are we to resume court at 12.00 or will you let us know whether the witness who is going to testify by video-conference link is available at that time or at some other time?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the sake of safety, I would prefer to let the Chamber know exactly when the witness is available so we don't waste any further time in our schedules for the day. And as soon as I can confirm that, I'll advise everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We're adjourned. --- Break taken at 9.44 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, who is the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: This next witness, Your Honours is the subject of protective measures. She's been granted face distortion and use of a pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Are we seeing her? It doesn't appear so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness testified by videolink].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may begin, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'd like to ask the Registry officer beside you to show you a piece of paper; and on that piece of paper, I hope you'll see your name and a witness number, being the number W-32.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I have the identical pseudonym sheet for display here in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Have you been given that piece of paper, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And is the name that you see on the paper in front you your first name and surname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: If we could have that marked, please, as the first exhibit under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes P527, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, next, Witness, I'd like to ask you in preparing to come to the office to testify today, did you have a chance to review your two previous statements; one to your own authorities and one to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, having read those statements, do you have any changes to make to them at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And if I was to ask you the same questions as investigators in 1995 and 2006 asked you, would your answers be the same as those that you have in those statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Yes, they would be the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: That being the case, then, Your Honours, if could have the statement, ter number 03060 and the further statement, ter number 03059, marked as the next exhibits under seal, that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll admit 65 ter number 03060 as P528, under seal; and 65 ter number 03059 as P529, also under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I would like to ask you a couple of questions clarifying some of the things that you spoke about in your earlier statements. The first one is this: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Is that part of Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: All right. Now, in your statement from 1996, you said that your old house was very close to the confrontation line, and you were constantly afraid of shelling and sniping. Is that why you moved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could you tell us why you decided to go back to your house on the day you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: I was moving during those days. I hadn't taken all of my things, so I came to get some of the things that were still left behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, to go back to your old house, what route would you normally take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: I went through cellars.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And why was that? Did you hear my question, Witness? Why did you go through cellars to get to your old house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Oh, to the apartment. Because there was shooting at ground floor level, so we went through cellars so as to avoid the main entrance.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Why did you go to the main door instead of going through the cellars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Because it was peaceful; there was no shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: What was the weather like on the day you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: It was warm. The weather was nice.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Was it a cloudy day or a clear day; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the weather was nice. It was sunny and I wore light clothes only. As far as I can remember, it was sunny.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Edgerton, just maybe for my own benefit, how did she go through cellars to get to her house? Are the cellars in an apartment complex, or isn't a cellar specific to a particular house? Maybe she can explain.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Did you hear the question of the Judge, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: It wasn't a house. It was an apartment building, and an apartment in that apartment building. In every apartment building, there is an entrance through which you go into a cellar, or the cellars.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, were these cellars connected at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So can you explain how you would travel from one cellar to the next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Every entrance had a cellar of its own, so my entrance had a back entrance into the cellar, and I used that entrance to get in and go upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Is that --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Does that clarify things for Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, as you went -- tell me if you're okay, if you need a break, Witness. But I will be very short now for the rest of the questions. As you went to the front door of your house, do you remember whether there were other civilians in the outside area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Yes. There was a woman, and there was a man who was guarding the area, saying that we shouldn't go that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And why was -- why was he saying that you shouldn't go that way; do you know? What exactly was he saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: He was standing there in order for people not to go to the other neighbourhood. There was sniper fire there, and he was warning people not to go there because they could get shot by sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I don't have any further questions for you, and now the counsel for General Milosevic is going examine you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. First, regarding the video, I'd like to know whether we are going to see it. This is part of a video that will be offered, I think, eventually as evidence. And personally I will oppose the admission if we haven't seen this video with the witness and if I haven't been given the opportunity of cross-examining the witness about this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't understand. No application has made in respect of a video. What are you opposing?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This video is part of an exhibit which, if I understood right, will be eventually admitted, once all the videos have been seen. Up until now, we always saw the clip -- video clips with the witnesses and Defence was given the opportunity to cross-examine the witness on the videos that were shown to them. And here the videos obviously are obviously on the list but we're not going to see them. So if I'm not given the opportunity to cross-examine, I'm just forewarning my colleagues on the other side that Defence eventually will oppose the admission of this part of the video that has not been seen. I believe that the video must be seen first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And that's an objection that I would uphold, but let me hear from the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, you haven't heard a request for the tender of this video because it is not my intention to tender the video through this witness but through the investigator who took the video and appears on the video with the witness, investigator Hogan, who will be testifying later in the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But it may very well be that the video should be shown now in the interest of everybody. The accused may have an interest in seeing and asking questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, we can play it here in the courtroom, Your Honour, and we just probably have to communicate with Sarajevo to see if they are in a position to play it for the witness on whatever software they have available to them. But we have it ready to play here in the courtroom for the benefit of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the counsel for Defence is right in asking this video to be shown to all of us. And this actually is in line with my concern of yesterday when I said that Prosecution must, first and foremost, establish the reality of the incident, the fact that this was an incident, that there was another that was victim actually shot. But the Prosecution must also establish the origin of the shots, and the video here is going to come in -- is going to be very helpful to show us exactly what the environment was, what the circumstances was surrounding this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Ms. Edgerton, we want to see it, and we have to see it. How soon can it be ready, bearing in mind that today we are stopping in a spirit of collegiality at 1.15 to accommodate another Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It is ready to play in this courtroom now, Your Honours. I will just wait to hear from Mr. Registrar about the ability to play it in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So I'm being told that the video is already in evidence. May I ask the legal officer, are you sure it's this particular video with this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Prosecutor, is this video already in evidence? Or the court deputy?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I can only indicate to the best of my information this clip hasn't been specifically tendered. The video as a whole already has an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe I could be of help. We've already discussed this because we've already seen a number of clips in this entire bundle of videos, and we were told then that we will be waiting for all witnesses involved in these videos to have been heard before the videos were actually offered for admission. Maybe the -- Ms. Edgerton can help us here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But can we get back to the present matter. I'm not a technical person, but would the witness in Sarajevo be able to see this video?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, according to my records, this particular clip is not already in evidence. A different clip from the same collection of videos is what is in evidence. Secondly, as to whether or not the witness in Sarajevo can see the video, I do believe it is possible, but I suggest that we do a quick test first of all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us proceed with the quick test.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Is it being broadcast, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, unfortunately that was just broadcast, and we're going to need to redact that portion of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That is to be redacted. What is the position, it can or cannot be seen in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It can be seen in Sarajevo. Perhaps then we could go into private session, and then play the video while the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's get it right now. We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Witness. I would like you to assist the Chamber in explaining where exactly the -- you believe the shots came from. When you, on the video, pointed in the direction of the fire, what I saw on the video was a two or three-storey white apartment building, which was just across the street, and my question is: Is that the building or the place where you think the shots came from, or did the shots come from a point farther away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The shots came from a place that was further away. There was shooting come from between the houses. There were these houses near the airport, and that is where the gun-fire was coming from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I don't know if we may wish to see the video again. But, do you, Witness, have a rough estimation of the distance to those houses and the place where you stood at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's difficult to say. I didn't go approximate that far. I would say about 100 metres, but I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Can I now tender that video clip as the next exhibit, and it should be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll admit that as P530, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, good afternoon, Witness. My name is Branislava Isailovic. I am a member of the Paris Bar Association, and I am defending Dragomir Milosevic in this case. As the Prosecutor has already told you, I'm about to ask you a few questions about what you have said today and about the content of your statements. First question relating to this video. It seemed to me that you were together with the investigator of the OTP in front of the door of a garage; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Where is this garage located as far as the rest of the building is concerned? Could you enter through here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Yes. I passed the garage in order to get into the hallway.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as confrontation lines are concerned, those you mentioned - and we shall get back to what you have talked about in your statement - where were the confrontation lines in relation to the houses which are opposite the building which is your building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: I don't know. This was behind the building. I don't know where exactly. I know where the sniper was firing from, but I don't know where exactly because I didn't go over there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask the registrar who is in Sarajevo, as well as my case manager, to display document 2830 which is on the 65 ter list. This is a document which is on the Defence list, and it's document 1D.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you see this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to find your way around on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: I don't think so. No, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would have liked to tender this map into evidence. Because on the basis of the rest of the evidence, I would like to establish the fact that because this witness does not remember the current name of the street, but on the basis of the rest of the evidence, the Defence will try to establish where on this map the house in question is located. This map also indicates where the confrontation lines are, those that were established by UNPROFOR. This map is part of a series of maps prepared by the Office of the Prosecutor, so may I suggest that this be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think Judge Harhoff will try with the witness to see whether the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Maybe I should just leave it to counsel, because I think it feels a bit empty to admit a map without any indication of the witness. So I wonder if the witness, with a little assistance, could perhaps understand the features or could be brought to understand the features of the map, and with some guidance could find the area in which she lived and maybe the street and maybe even the place in the street. The witness seems to be perfectly capable of understanding what is on the map, if, perhaps, she gets a little assistance. So I would like to you try, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please examine this map and try to get your bearings and find the Dobrinja area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We also need the help of somebody in Sarajevo to help us get to understand what the witness is showing us on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you at least see the Dobrinja area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Have you found where Dobrinja is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you circle the entire area of Dobrinja, please, and then we shall try and locate your building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-32
utterances.text: I do it like this, like this, can I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, please be careful in relation to her giving any evidence that might identify her.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see what the witness has marked on the map, please? So I believe we need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We have no objection going into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for giving it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until tomorrow, 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 5th day of April, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.04 p.m.,
